description: From the link premise (part (a): if Jesus holds a mandate from g and founded the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, a governing power he gave or promised makes that founding one in the mandate; part (b), on teaching, is unused), the premise that John 20.21-23's commission saying is independent of Matthew 18.17-18's or Matthew 16.18-19's, and the criterion of multiple attestation for the heaven-ratified family only (two distinct independent reports of the family ⇒ Jesus gave or promised some power of it), it follows that wherever Jesus holds a mandate from g, founded the Catholic Church and it is visible with authority, the message rival is false. It is not a transcription: no premise has the conclusion as its consequent; the proof combines the independence premise with the reported powers (the family is reported in Matthew 16, 18 and John 20; the strand labels are informational and unused by the proof) to meet the criterion's antecedent, uses the classification that every heaven-ratified power is governing to meet the link premise's antecedent, and only then contradicts the rival; with another family or another classification it would fail. The checked content is thin and should be read so: it is the sourced powers list and the stipulated classifications (Power.Governing, HeavenRatified); the independence and criterion premises are tailored to exactly this family and these report pairs, and the link premise's consequent is what the rival denies. Each premise is needed by an omission model, and the premises are jointly satisfiable. It verifies consequence only: all three premises are open, and the independence and criterion premises have no source. The result does not refute the rival, which may deny any premise, and it does not establish STMT-COMMISSION-REPORTS-GO-BACK-TO-JESUS (CommissionAttestation.attestation_not_reports). Its conclusion is used by no argument reaching the root.
